description: Identifies where in the supply chain OTIF failures originate by tagging each late case with its first deviation from the expected timeline. Built for TMS / WMS / OMS multi-table exports. The happy path is: Order Released → Carrier Tendered → Picked Up → In Transit → Delivered On Time. Late cases deviate at Carrier Tendered (acceptance failure), Pick Up (dwell), In Transit (transit time), or Delivered (last mile). Slice by carrier, lane (origin/destination pair), and warehouse_id to locate systemic failure points.

required_tables.name: shipments
required_tables.description: Shipment / load records (shipment_id, order_id, origin_warehouse, destination_zip, carrier_id, lane_id, mode, requested_delivery_date, status)
required_tables.source_hint: TMS shipment master or OMS fulfillment export

required_tables.name: tender_events
required_tables.description: Carrier tender and acceptance events (shipment_id, tendered_at, carrier_id, tender_outcome, accepted_at, rejection_reason)
required_tables.source_hint: TMS tender log; one row per tender attempt

required_tables.name: tracking_events
required_tables.description: Milestone tracking updates from carrier or IoT (shipment_id, event_type, event_at, location, carrier_code)
required_tables.source_hint: Carrier tracking API feed or EDI 214 events; filter to: PICKUP, IN_TRANSIT, OUT_FOR_DELIVERY, DELIVERED

sample_kpis: Dwell time at origin (Released → Picked Up)
On-time delivery rate by carrier and lane
notes: First-deviation tagging: the conformance deviations table identifies the first non-conforming transition per case. Join that to carrier_id, lane_id, and origin_warehouse (via additional_columns) in a BI tool to produce the root-cause breakdown. The filter fields on Picked Up, In Transit, and Delivered are advisory — if your tracking feed has one row per event type with different event_type codes, use the connector WHERE clause to materialize those as separate tables before upload, or use the Extraction Copilot to melt the event_type column.
